findings: This is not an interim/H1/Q2 2026 results RNS. It is an Investegate-hosted regulatory/product announcement (dated 2026-07-29 in task metadata) for FDA De Novo classification of the TESSA Spatial Surgery System — it does not close the missing Aug 2026 interim results gap.
Body type: FDA De Novo clearance announcement for TESSA (Tracking Enabled Spatial Surgery Assistant) Spatial Surgery System, not financial results or trading update.

Regulatory pathway: FDA granted De Novo classification (not 510(k)). TESSA is described as the first device in a new FDA category for intra-articular orthopedic stereotaxic navigation instruments, establishing a regulatory reference point for future innovations.

Indication for use: femoral anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) surgery of the knee. The system assists placement and navigation of the femoral tunnel using augmented reality; broader arthroscopic applications are anticipated over time.
Clinical context cited: femoral malposition (29%) and tibial malposition (11%) are among the most common reasons for ACLR failure (source: Li X et al., Int Orthop 2023, referenced in body).

Sports Medicine positioning: framed as a generational advance and category-defining spatial surgery solution; positions Smith+Nephew as a leader in personalised, data-enabled, digital Sports Medicine. Quote from Scott Schaffner, President of Global Sports Medicine.

Technology: preoperative MR/CT scans with cloud-based deep-learning on AWS; NVIDIA AI infrastructure; overlays patient-specific 3D bone model onto live 4K arthroscopic video for real-time navigation. Technology originated from Perceive3D S.A. (University of Coimbra spin-off), acquired by Smith+Nephew.

Commercial timing: TESSA will be commercially introduced in Q3 2026 with focus on early customer adoption; increased deployment expected in 2027. No revenue, uptake, volume, or reimbursement/pricing language for TESSA.
No H1/Q2 2026 financial metrics, underlying growth rates, or trading commentary appear in this document.

Forward-looking statements disclaimer: standard Smith+Nephew boilerplate noting statements may not prove accurate; identifies risks including regulatory approvals, reimbursement decisions, product defects/recalls, litigation, supply chain disruption, competition for personnel, acquisitions, cybersecurity, FX, and other political/economic factors; references Form 20-F; no obligation to update forward-looking statements.
